## Purpose and boundary

`acr-scott-custom` is an explicitly selected global model, not a new default
forecasting policy. It estimates peer-group references and produces a separate
recursive forecast for every series. It does not tie results to EG targets,
enforce segment growth ordering, redistribute pricing mix, or use an LLM.

The engine combines same-month historical growth with recent and peer growth,
damps historical growth relative to the current revenue base, and applies the
selected source-derived caps and calendar overrides. Supporting `lm()` fits
forecast reference growth and dispersion, not individual-series revenue.
Forecast accuracy must be assessed with held-out actuals; a rule-based forecast
is not guaranteed to outperform ARIMA, ETS or seasonal naive.

## Required data

- Monthly dates in a `Date` column, with a consistent monthly convention.
- Explicit `combo_variables` defining unique bottom-level series.
- Nonnegative, finite targets: monthly revenue totals or average daily rates.
- At least two series, each with seven consecutive observed months through the
  training cutoff. Three seasonal analogues need substantially longer history.
- `pool_by`: a nonempty subset of the combo variables. Product, geography and
  segment names are not hard-coded.
- Monthly totals use calendar days unless `exposure` names a strictly positive
  adjusted-days column with historical and future values. Daily-rate targets
  use exposure one and return daily-rate forecasts.

Missing historical targets and internal gaps are errors. Leading unavailable
months introduced by FinnTS padding are explicitly excluded from the model.
An actual zero remains an observation; a zero final revenue rate cannot recover
under this multiplicative model without a separately approved policy.

The first version requires `stationary = FALSE`, `box_cox = FALSE`,
`clean_outliers = FALSE`, `clean_missing_values = FALSE`, `forecast_approach =
"bottoms_up"`, and R1. Incompatible settings are rejected, not silently changed.
Do not mix parent totals and their component series in the peer population.
Spark certification and automatic Agent discovery/configuration are out of scope.

## Dynamic pooling

`pool_by = c("Product", "Segment")` shares references across all other dimensions.
Adding `Region` or `PricingLevel` to `combo_variables` creates finer series without
changing that pooling definition. A different run can instead use
`pool_by = c("Service", "CustomerTier")`.

`pool_fallbacks` is an ordered list of nonempty, strictly coarser subsets. The
first level with `min_pool_series` usable distinct series is used; the default
minimum is three. For example, `list(c("Product", "Segment"), "Product")` can
follow `pool_by = c("Product", "Segment", "CustomerType")`. No other dimensions
are dropped automatically. With no adequate pool, `insufficient_pool = "error"`
is the default. Explicit `"series"` fallback uses within-series references and
is recorded as different from peer pooling.

Statistics use equally weighted finite growth observations within the most
recent three years, excluding growth outside the source's open (-3, 3) interval.
Adding detail can therefore change the observation mix. Overall references group
by peer identity; monthly references also group by actual calendar month/year.
They are not revenue-weighted and do not pool all Julys into one monthly point.

## Configuration and example

The following is a template, not an executed example. `input` is the user's
monthly data frame and includes future adjusted days if that option is selected.
Options are specified once in preparation and persisted canonically in the run
log. Changed effective settings require a new run.

```{r workflow, eval=FALSE}
library(finnts)

options <- list(
  pool_by = c("Product", "Segment"),
  pool_fallbacks = list(),
  min_pool_series = 3L,
  insufficient_pool = "error",
  target_mode = "monthly_total",
  exposure = "AdjustedDays",
  profile = "standard",
  calendar_policy = "scott_main"
)

run <- set_run_info(path = output_directory)
forecast_time_series(
  run_info = run, input_data = input,
  combo_variables = c("Product", "Segment", "Region"),
  target_variable = "Revenue", date_type = "month", forecast_horizon = 12,
  hist_end_date = cutoff,
  models_to_run = c("acr-scott-custom", "arima", "ets", "snaive"),
  recipes_to_run = "R1", stationary = FALSE, box_cox = FALSE,
  clean_missing_values = FALSE, clean_outliers = FALSE,
  acr_scott_custom_options = options, run_global_models = TRUE,
  run_local_models = TRUE, run_ensemble_models = FALSE,
  average_models = FALSE, return_data = FALSE
)
```

`profile` is `standard` or `high_growth`. Alternatively, `profile_column` names
a column containing those values, constant within each series. No profile is
inferred from product names. `calendar_policy` explicitly selects `scott_main`,
`scott_pricing`, or `none`. Both Scott presets amplify negative July growth by
dividing by 0.85. In December, `scott_main` multiplies positive growth by 0.85,
whereas `scott_pricing` divides negative growth by 0.85. Overrides follow caps.

`list_models()` retains the default inventory. Use
`list_models(include_opt_in = TRUE)` to see the new selectable name. Other models
can train locally in the same run. Custom-only selections do not launch empty
local jobs. A run that disables global training or contains only one series
cannot use this model.

When launching from RStudio with `callr::rscript()`, include the library
containing the custom FinnTS build in `libpath` before the child starts.
Changing only `.libPaths()` or `R_LIBS` inside the child is insufficient for
this launcher: its generated startup configuration can make PSOCK workers load
a different FinnTS installation. Do not detach/reload competing FinnTS versions
in an existing session. The coordinator and all workers must load the same
installed build; installed parallel-preparation regression coverage checks this.

## Active rule contract

Let `oldest`, `middle`, and `latest` denote the same calendar month three, two,
and one years ago. Quality is absolute distance from the peer median divided by
peer standard deviation. Signed scores remain available for the branches that
explicitly require positive deviations. Equal-quality ties choose the oldest
available year. Missing years are not zero-valued candidates.

Every growth result is converted recursively to the next daily rate and then,
for monthly totals, multiplied by exposure. Negative resulting rates are floored
to zero; diagnostics retain both proposed and effective growth.

Standard branches, in order:

| Rule | Condition and formula before its source cap |
|---|---|
| 1 | Latest quality > 2 and best quality > 2: damped reference median; when latest growth is negative, blend 65% damped median and 35% median plus one monthly dispersion. |
| 2 | Latest quality > 2 but a better year exists: 60% best analogue + 40% reference, damped using the latest historical base. |
| 3 | Best quality > 1.5: the same 60/40 blend. |
| 4 | Best quality > 1: 70% best analogue + 30% reference. |
| 5_1 | Older qualities < 2, latest growth negative and both older years positive: 20% oldest + 45% middle + 25% latest + 10% reference, with per-year damping. |
| 5_4 | All three qualities < 0.8: 15% oldest + 30% middle + 55% latest, with per-year damping. |
| 5_5 | Latest/oldest qualities < 1.5, latest positive and oldest negative: 25% oldest + 70% latest + 5% reference. |
| 5_year | Best analogue is an older year: 95% analogue + 5% reference, damped using that year's base. |
| 10 | Available latest-year growth times latest-base damping. |
| 11 | Historical peer median when no usable seasonal formula remains. |

Standard damping is `clip(1.06 * historical_base / previous_rate, 0.1, 0.9)`;
the oldest term of rules 5_1/5_4 retains factor 0.96. Rules 1-4 and 5_year use
monthly dispersion caps. Rules 5_1/5_4/5_5/10 use overall dispersion; rule 11
retains its uncapped source fallback. Caps are reference median +/- two dispersions.

High-growth branches, in order:

| Rule | Condition and formula |
|---|---|
| 1 | No latest growth: (60% recent + 40% reference) * 0.78. |
| 2/3 | Only latest available and quality > 3 / > 2: damp 60% recent + 40% reference, or 40% recent + 20% latest + 40% reference. |
| 4-6 / 9-11 | Latest sign opposes both older years: depending on older qualities, use oldest/middle/latest weights 30/55/15, middle/latest 80/20, or latest/reference 30/70, with per-year damping. |
| 7_1/7_2/8 | Latest negative, middle positive: use middle/reference 80/20, latest/middle/reference 10/80/10, or latest/reference 15/85 according to quality. |
| 12/13 | Latest positive, middle negative, oldest absent: latest/middle/reference 10/80/10 if middle quality < 1.5; otherwise latest/reference 15/85. |
| 14 | Only two years, both signed scores > 3: damp 60% recent + 40% reference. |
| 15 | Only two years, both signed scores > 1.5: damp 65% recent + 45.5% reference + 10% latest + 5% middle. Weights intentionally are not normalized. |
| 15_1/15_2 | Middle quality > 2 and latest quality < 1 / < 2: 90/10 or 75/25 damped latest / previous-month reference. |
| 16 | Remaining two-year cases: per-year damped latest/middle 70/30. |
| 17 | Latest quality < 1: 10% recent + damped (85% latest + 5% reference). |
| 18/19 | Latest plus middle/oldest quality < 1.5: 10% recent + damped (50% latest + 30% middle + 5% reference), or (60% latest + 20% oldest + 5% reference). |
| 20/21 | Middle/oldest quality < 2: 20% recent + damped (65% middle + 15% reference), or 25% recent + damped (55% oldest + 20% reference). |
| 22 | 50% recent + 50% damped reference. |

High-growth damping uses factor 0.98. Rules 4-13, 15_1, 15_2 and 16 use the
source overall-dispersion cap; the other high-growth branches are not universally
capped. Source product-name exclusions are not inferred for generalized inputs;
profile selection is explicit and needs confirmation during sample review.

The implementation intentionally corrects missing-as-zero analogue selection,
ambiguous selected-year identity, the skipped recent month, and reference trend
index/predictor/dispersion errors. The latest complete 12-month reference window
predicts positions 13 onward. Missing/nonfinite trends and negative dispersion
predictions fall back to valid training references. Dead negative-quality and
shadowed branches are not silently activated. These changes are not claimed to
be bit-identical to the original application.

## Artifacts and explanations

The fitted global workflow is stored normally with model ID
`acr-scott-custom--global--R1` and `Combo_ID = "All-Data"`. Per-series global
forecast files retain normal FinnTS naming. No model code reads Scott's script,
opens spreadsheets, writes debug files, launches clusters or mutates fitted state.

`explain_acr_scott_custom(fitted_workflow, future_predictors)` returns forecasts,
rules, peer/fallback identity, available analogue values, quality, weights,
damping, reference levels, caps and calendar effects. Original-unit forecasts
are not statistical confidence bounds. Existing FinnTS interval/selection policy
is unchanged. Required typed dimension metadata is preserved in R1 and removed
before other models or feature selection see it.

## Manual historical-data checkpoint

After synthetic integration succeeds, provide a local CSV or RDS and the column
mappings above, preferably two groups with three series each and 61-73 months.
Confirm adjusted-day availability at historical origins, profile/calendar policy,
and an output directory outside the repository. Historical gaps, duplicates,
negative values, ambiguous units or aggregate/child mixtures require correction
or a revised model policy before evaluation.

The repository script `tools/validate-acr-scott-custom.R` accepts a local RDS
configuration with `input_path`, `output_dir`, `date_column`, `target_variable`,
`combo_variables`, `options`, and optional `holdout`/`horizon` (default 12).
It excludes the final holdout from fitting, runs the custom model alongside
ARIMA/ETS/seasonal naive through FinnTS, and saves per-series/peer metrics,
separately labeled portfolio-total metrics, plots, forecasts, rule explanations,
and saved workflows. WMAPE is NA when the actual denominator is zero. It refuses
nonempty output directories and does not change the input file.

Review a standard and a high-growth/edge series before sign-off. A worse result
than a baseline is evidence, not a reason to force this model to win. Broader
policies, new cadences, transformation support or different branch weights need
separate approval. The full deterministic package suite and correctly configured
R CMD check follow any sample-driven approved repairs; a synthetic-only run is
not a claim that real business forecasts have been validated.
